latest.content:

10 August 2026
Angus Energy PLC
("Angus Energy", the "Company" or together with its subsidiaries, the "Group")
(AIM:ANGS)
Accelerated Debt Reduction
·
Initial cash sweep completed following the successful financial restructuring
·
ORRI Cash Amount of £1.95 million repaid in full
·
Additional £1.996 million prepayment made to the Trafigura facility
·
Total debt repayments of £5.241 million since 24 June 2026, demonstrating the Company's accelerating deleveraging strategy
·
Future cash sweeps will now be applied entirely towards accelerating repayment of the Trafigura facility
·
Demonstrates the cash-generative strength of the business and validates the recently completed restructuring
·
Further strengthens the balance sheet while supporting continued investment in growth alongside accelerated deleveraging
The Company is pleased to announce that, following completion of its recently announced financial restructuring, it has completed the first cash sweep under the amended financing arrangements.
Completion of the first cash sweep has enabled the Company to repay the £1.95 million ORRI Cash Amount in full, eliminating this liability entirely, while also making a £1.996 million prepayment against the Trafigura senior debt facility. As a result, the outstanding Trafigura facility has reduced to approximately £22.7 million.
Since announcing the restructuring on 26 June 2026, the Company has repaid a total of £5.241 million of debt principal, materially strengthening the Group's balance sheet. This rapid reduction in indebtedness demonstrates the Company's ability to generate cash while executing its strategy of accelerating deleveraging and continuing to invest in future growth.
The repayment of the ORRI Cash Amount represents an important milestone. Under the amended financing arrangements, all future cash sweep proceeds will now be directed exclusively towards reducing the outstanding Trafigura facility, accelerating the Company's deleveraging profile.
Carlos Fernandes, Finance Director, commented:
"The completion of our first cash sweep demonstrates that our restructuring strategy is already delivering tangible results. We have significantly strengthened the balance sheet, eliminated the ORRI liability and reduced the Trafigura facility, while continuing to invest in the business.
Every pound of debt we repay reduces future financing obligations and increases the value attributable to shareholders. With future cash sweeps now directed entirely towards the Trafigura facility, we are well positioned to continue accelerating deleveraging while executing our operational growth strategy."
END

Angus Energy PLC

(AIM:ANGS)
Annual Maintenance Shutdown Completion
·
Annual maintenance shutdown completed safely, with no accidents, injuries or harm to the environment.
·
Production resumed intermittently on 28th July 2026 and now up to full capacity, following the successful completion of the annual maintenance programme.
Annual Maintenance Programme Completed
Further to the Company's announcement of 15 July 2026 regarding the planned annual maintenance shutdown at the Saltfleetby Gas Field, Angus Energy is pleased to confirm that the programme has been successfully completed.
The maintenance shutdown, together with the associated programme of subsurface data acquisition, was completed safely, with no accidents, injuries or harm to the environment.
Production resumed on 28th July 2026 and ramped up to full capacity on August 4th, 2026. As part of the normal post-maintenance recommissioning process, the Company has been progressively returning the facilities to full operating capacity. Current production now exceeding the pre-shut down rates due to a combination of flush production from the shut-ins and more efficient operations post maintenance activity.
The Company thanks its employees and contractors for the safe and successful execution of the programme.
END

Second Quarter 2026 Production, Operations, Corporate and Finance Update
·

barrels of gas condensate.

·

·
Revenues driven primarily by higher realised gas prices, improved hedging position and increased production volumes.
·
Production uplift driven by successful completion of Saltfleetby workovers.
·
First principal repayment of £1.29 million made under the Group's senior debt facility with Trafigura, reducing outstanding borrowings to £24.7 million at 30 June 2026.
Production and Operations Update
Saltfleetby
Gas sales from the Saltfleetby Field totalled 5.85 million therms during April, May and June 2026, compared to 5.24 million therms in the first quarter of 2026. This increase was driven by the successful completion of the Saltfleetby well workover programme.
Average monthly gas sales for the quarter were 1.95 million therms, up from 1.75 million therms in Q1 2026. Gas condensate production averaged 113 barrels per day, compared to 111 barrels per day in the previous quarter. Operational efficiency was 91% which is a slight increase following the impact of workover interventions on two of the three producing wells (Q1 2026: 87%)
.
Saltfleetby Planned Maintenance
During July, the Company will undertake its planned annual maintenance shutdown alongside a programme of facility optimisation activities and subsurface data acquisition. As a result, production is expected to be intermittently impacted over a period of approximately 7 days with a full site shut down for an additional 7 days as the works are carried out. Normal production is expected to resume following completion of the programme.
Brockham
Total oil production from the Brockham Field for the quarter was 4,027 barrels, equating to an average production rate of 44 barrels per day, broadly in line with the previous quarter (Q1 2026: 4,114 barrels; 46 barrels per day). Operational efficiency was 100% (Q1 2026: 100%).
The Company is progressing preparations to restart production from the BRX4z well targeting the Portland reservoir.
Finance Update
Estimated revenues for the quarter were £7.16 million (Q1 2026: £5.24 million), representing an increase of approximately 37%, driven primarily by higher realised gas prices, increased production volumes and improved hedging position.
As at 30 June 2026, outstanding borrowings under the Group's senior debt facility with Trafigura had reduced to £24.7 million (31 March 2026: £26.0 million), following the Group's first principal repayment of £1.29 million.
END

company_30s.what_they_do: Angus Energy Plc is a small, UK‑based oil and gas exploration and production company that focuses on the North Sea. It extracts natural gas and condensate from its own fields, delivering the product to the market and to its own storage facilities.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The North Sea remains a key source of European gas, and Angus holds a modest but strategically located field that could help meet regional supply needs. Its low‑cost, mature assets give it a niche advantage against larger rivals, and any uptick in production can ripple through the supply chain and attract institutional interest.
company_30s.current_state: The company is in a rebuilding phase after a major maintenance shutdown and a debt‑reduction program. It has recently appointed new directors, disclosed major holdings, and is preparing for the next production update. Its share price sits at a very small fraction of its all‑time high, signalling that the market has largely discounted the company’s recent performance.

rns_narrative: The first theme is operational stabilization: a completed maintenance shutdown and a push to reduce debt show the company is trimming costs and protecting cash flow.

The second theme is governance and capital structure: new directors and major holdings filings suggest a reshaped board and a more focused shareholder base, which could bring fresh capital or strategic partnerships.

The third theme is production focus: a series of updates on output and a forthcoming interim results release indicate the company is gearing up to demonstrate a production uptick that could reignite investor interest.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet skepticism with a flicker of cautious hope – the community is largely silent but a few posts hint at a potential rebound.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: A handful of traders praise the recent production fluctuations and hint that a successful workover could push output higher, potentially turning the stock around.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Critics point to management’s history of cutting production when prices rise and raise concerns over limited on‑site storage, suggesting the company might still struggle to monetize its output.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: Overall sentiment remains flat; the few bullish voices are not yet gaining traction, so the market is still waiting for a clear catalyst.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for the ticker is dead, meaning the stock has no recent search interest – a classic contrarian signal that the market is unaware of any upcoming news.

near_term_catalysts: The next production and operations update on 15th July could reveal higher output numbers – a jump of even 10% would be newsworthy.
Any announcement of new financing or a partnership to increase storage capacity would address current operational concerns.
A significant volume spike on the day the company releases its interim results would confirm that the market is paying attention.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a clear break above the recent support level with accompanying volume above the 20‑day average. A sudden uptick in production figures or a new capital raise would also validate the mean‑reversion thesis.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early stages of a deep crash cycle – the APEX score suggests a tight compression but the price is still far below its peak. A bounce will likely need a catalyst that restores confidence in production and cash flow.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: If the company can lift production by even 10% and secure a short‑term financing deal, the share could climb to 50% of its previous high – a 300‑400% upside from today. The historical record of deep crashes delivering large rebounds supports this view.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The company still faces operational risks: limited storage, a history of cutting output when prices rise, and a fragile balance sheet. If it fails to raise capital or if production stalls, the share could remain trapped near the current level.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside is several times the current price, while the downside is capped at the current level because the share is already at a 86% drawdown. The asymmetry is high: a 300% gain versus a 0% loss if the market remains unchanged.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter on a breakout above the 0.00p support with a stop 10% below that level. Size the position to 5–10% of discretionary capital, using a trailing stop to lock in gains as the price climbs.
playbook.if_watching: Hold cash until the next production update or a clear volume spike. Trigger a buy if the share closes above the 20‑day moving average with volume 1.5× the average.
playbook.if_passing: Only consider abandoning the position if the company announces a delisting notice or a bankruptcy filing, which would eliminate upside potential.

ai_insights.bottom_line: Angus Energy sits at a deep 86% crash, yet the market’s silence and the company’s operational reset create a high‑reward, low‑loss contrarian play that could see the share rebound to half its peak in the next few months.
